interface.doc: The destination latent where frames will be replaced.
The source latent providing frames to insert into the destination latent. If not provided, the destination latent is returned unchanged.
The starting latent frame index in the destination latent where the source latent frames will be placed. Negative values count from the end.

sourceSchemas.description: Allows setting advanced options for the Chroma Radiance model.

interface.doc: When enabled, will delegate to an existing model function wrapper if it exists. Generally should be left enabled.
First sigma that these options will be in effect.
Last sigma that these options will be in effect.
Allows overriding the default NeRF tile size. -1 means use the default (32). 0 means use non-tiling mode (may require a lot of VRAM).

Force usage of sequential text token IDs instead of zeroes. Should be used for checkpoints from 2026-05-22 to 2026-06-01 that are trained in this way but do not contain the __sequential__ key in the state dict.

sourceSchemas.description: Uses the provided model, positive and negative conditioning to denoise the latent image.

interface.doc: The model used for denoising the input latent.
The random seed used for creating the noise.
The number of steps used in the denoising process.

The Classifier-Free Guidance scale balances creativity and adherence to the prompt. Higher values result in images more closely matching the prompt however too high values will negatively impact quality.
The algorithm used when sampling, this can affect the quality, speed, and style of the generated output.
The scheduler controls how noise is gradually removed to form the image.
The conditioning describing the attributes you want to include in the image.
The conditioning describing the attributes you want to exclude from the image.
The latent image to denoise.
The amount of denoising applied, lower values will maintain the structure of the initial image allowing for image to image sampling.
Only used for video VAEs: Amount of frames to encode at a time.
Only used for video VAEs: Amount of frames to overlap.
Only used for video VAEs: Amount of frames to decode at a time.
Only used for video VAEs: Amount of frames to overlap.

sourceSchemas.description: Pad a resized image for SeedVR2 model. Alpha channel is dropped. The node Post-Process SeedVR2 Output re-applies it from the original resized image.

interface.doc: The resized image to process.
The padded image for VAE encoding.

sourceSchemas.description: Align the generated image with the original resized image and apply color correction.

interface.doc: The generated image to process.
The original resized image before pre-processing, used as reference.

Method to match the generated image colors to the original image. lab: transfer color in CIELAB space, preserving detail (most faithful). wavelet: transfer low-frequency color, keeping upscaled high-frequency detail. adain: match per-channel mean/std (fastest, global tint). none: skip color transfer (geometry alignment only).
The aligned, color-corrected image.

sourceSchemas.description: Build SeedVR2 positive/negative conditioning from a VAE latent.

interface.doc: The SeedVR2 model.
The positive conditioning for sampling.
The negative conditioning for sampling.

sourceSchemas.description: Split a SeedVR2 video latent into overlapping temporal chunks small enough to sample one at a time within VRAM, wiring latents outputs to both Apply SeedVR2 Conditioning and the sampler latent input before recombining with Merge SeedVR2 Latents.

interface.doc: The VAE-encoded SeedVR2 latent to split.
Latent frames shared between adjacent chunks and crossfaded at merge; 0 = no overlap.
Pixel frames per temporal chunk (4n+1: 1, 5, 9, 13, ...).
The temporal chunks in sequence order.
The effective latent-frame overlap between adjacent chunks, for Merge SeedVR2 Latents.

sourceSchemas.description: Recombine sampled SeedVR2 latent temporal chunks into one latent, crossfading each overlap with a Hann window sized by the temporal_overlap wired from Split SeedVR2 Latent.

interface.doc: The sampled temporal chunks in sequence order.
The temporal_overlap output of Split SeedVR2 Latent. 0 = plain concatenation.
The recombined full-length latent.
